real_conflicts: The expressiveness proposal to add 'subtle, genre-specific background tints' to individual event cells directly harms my mandate. Introducing 8+ different background colors into a strict chronological grid will destroy the visual rhythm, make the rows harder to scan, and fragment the schedule into a chaotic patchwork rather than a coherent system.
accepted: The brief_intent proposal to reduce the number of performances per stage is strongly accepted. Reducing the row count is the single most effective way to improve legibility and allow the 'meaningful grouping' of time slots to breathe.
The visual_system_craft proposal to increase the width of the vertical stage-color bars is accepted, as it reinforces the column boundaries I identified as weak in my initial critique.
concession: I concede that the current genre labels are too passive. While I oppose changing the background of the cells, I agree that the genre text itself needs to be more prominent to satisfy the 'meaningful connection' requirement without breaking the grid.
compromise: Instead of adding background tints to the cells, we will apply the 'genre-specific' color coding to the genre text itself. For example, 'Psychedelic' text will be a soft purple, 'Americana' a warm orange, etc. This adds the requested visual rhythm and differentiation while keeping the background uniform and the grid structure intact.
nonnegotiable: The chronological alignment of the time column and the distinct, high-contrast styling of the headliner row must remain the primary structural anchors of the page.
